# cert/map

> Open-source roadmap and study organiser for cybersecurity certifications: 320 cybersecurity certifications mapped across 17 domains and four seniority tiers, each with its current exam price, prerequisites and renewal cycle, and for the most sought-after ones an ordered study plan with exam guides, courses, reading, direct links to free practice labs, open-source projects and practice questions. Compare two certifications side by side, build a personal roadmap, annotate it and share it with a link.

cert/map is a community-maintained reference for the cybersecurity certification landscape and a tool for planning how to study for it. It answers three questions: which certification to take (the roadmap and the comparisons), in what order (roadmaps ordered by prerequisite, with cost and study time), and how to prepare each one (study plans whose links are checked). The entire dataset lives in CSV files under `data/`; the browser parses them at load time, so the data is also directly machine-readable for anyone integrating it. The site is at https://certmap.dev/.

## Vendors covered

8kSec, Altered Security, APIsec University, arcX, AWS, Basel Institute, Cellebrite, Centri, Chainalysis, Check Point, Cisco, CNCF, CompTIA, Coursera, CREST, CrowdStrike, CSA, CWNP, CyberDefenders, CyberWarFare Labs, DRI International, EC-Council, edX, Elastic, Fortinet, GIAC, GitHub, Google, Hack The Box, HashiCorp, IACIS, IAPP, INE, IntelTechniques, ISA, ISACA, ISC2, ISFCE, Juniper, Linux Foundation, LPI, Magnet Forensics, McAfee Institute, MCSI, Microsoft, OffSec, Okta, OpenText, OSINT Industries, OSMOSIS, Palo Alto Networks, PCI SSC, PECB, PeopleCert, PortSwigger, Practical DevSecOps, Red Hat, SABSA, SailPoint, Social Links, Splunk, TCM Security, The Open Group, The SecOps Group, TRM Labs, VMware, Wireshark, Zero-Point Security, Zscaler, zSecurity.

## Domain taxonomy

The roadmap groups certifications across seventeen domains:

- Communication & Network Security
- IAM
- Security Architecture & Engineering
- Asset Security
- Security & Risk Management
- Software Security
- Security Operations
- Cyber Threat Intelligence
- OSINT (open-source intelligence)
- Cloud/SysOps
- *nix
- ICS/IoT
- GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance)
- Forensics
- Incident Handling
- Penetration Testing
- Exploitation

## Seniority tiers

Each certification is placed at one of four tiers:

- **beginner**: foundational, no significant prerequisites
- **intermediate**: assumes one to three years of relevant experience
- **advanced**: specialised, three to five years
- **expert**: capstone hands-on credentials or executive-level certifications

## Dataset schema

`data/certs.csv` columns:

- `id`: slug, primary key (e.g. `oscp`, `cissp`)
- `name`: full official name
- `acronym`: short label
- `vendor`: issuing organisation
- `domain`: one of the domains listed above
- `level`: `beginner` | `intermediate` | `advanced` | `expert`
- `price_usd`: exam fee in USD (empty if unknown, `0` if free)
- `currency_note`: clarification when relevant (member/non-member, bundle, etc.)
- `duration_min`: exam length in minutes
- `validity_years`: renewal cycle; `0` or empty means lifetime
- `prerequisites`: semicolon-separated `id` values
- `dod_8140`: boolean for US DoD 8140 framework approval
- `url`: vendor's official certification page
- `description`: one to two factual sentences
- `tags`: semicolon-separated free-form tags
- `weight`: optional integer for intra-cell ordering in the matrix
- `restricted_to`: optional audience restriction (e.g. `Law enforcement only`)
- `exam_count`: number of separate exams required
- `renewal_cost`: renewal fee in USD when there is one
- `hands_on`: boolean, true for performance-based exams
- `price_verified_at`: date the price was last confirmed on the vendor's page
- `issuer`: organisation that awards the credential when it is not the vendor (course-platform certificates)

## Features of the live site

- **Study plans**: for each certification with resources, a numbered plan in four phases (know the exam, learn the material, practice hands-on, test yourself). Each plan has its own page at `certs/plan-<id>.html` and also appears in the roadmap's detail drawer and on the certification page, with each phase folding away.
- **Practice material**: direct links to TryHackMe rooms and paths, Hack The Box Academy modules, CyberDefenders labs and similar, plus open-source projects (vulnerable applications, lab builders, detection rules, forensic datasets). No exam content or exam write-ups are linked.
- **Comparisons**: side-by-side pages for the most searched pairs, in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Arabic, Korean and Hebrew.
- **Roadmap builder**: add certifications by search, see them as a list or as a graph of prerequisites, write a note on each step, name the roadmap and share it.
- **Matrix view**: 17 columns by 4 rows. Capstone certifications surface to the top of each cell via an optional weight value.
- **List view**: cards grouped by domain with vendor, level, tags and price visible.
- **Filters**: domain, level, vendor (with substring quick-search), price range, free-only, DoD 8140 only, no-prerequisites only, hands-on exam only, verified prices only.
- **Shareable roadmaps**: a selection can be named and shared as `r/#<id>,<id>?name=<title>` (which opens `#/roadmap/<id>,<id>` in the app); the link shows the ordered path with cost and study-time totals, as a list or as a graph of prerequisites, and carries any notes written on the steps.
- **Role paths**: each preset path (penetration tester, SOC analyst, cloud security architect and others) has a page at `certs/path-<role>.html`.
- **Course-based certificates**: programs from Coursera and edX are included with the platform as vendor and are described as course-based, with no proctored exam.
- **Static pages**: every certification has a plain HTML page at `certs/<id>.html`, and `certs/` lists them all by domain.
- **Detail drawer**: opens on click, deep-linkable as `#/cert/<id>`, lists prerequisites as clickable chips back to other certifications.
- **Path planner**: pick multiple certifications and the site sorts them by prerequisite and difficulty, then reports total cost, total study hours and approximate months at ten study-hours per week.
- **Delayed hover tooltip**: appears after a 450 ms hover and previews the cert's price, exam length, renewal cycle and prerequisites.
- **Light and dark themes**: dark by default.
- **Mobile layout**: drawer-style filter panel, single-column list, the matrix view collapses to the list.
- **Strict CSP**: `script-src 'self'` with a hashed JSON-LD island; no third-party scripts, no `unsafe-inline`.

## How prices and accuracy work

Most vendors do not publish their exam fees on public certification pages. The CSV records the last known list price in USD with a `currency_note` for member/non-member splits or training-bundle pricing. Pricing should always be confirmed with the vendor before purchase. Corrections are welcome via pull request against `data/certs.csv`.

## How to contribute

The whole dataset is a single CSV file. Editing it requires no JavaScript and no build step:

1. Fork the repository.
2. Edit `data/certs.csv`.
3. Run `npm run validate` to check the row.
4. Open a pull request. The CI workflow runs the same validator.

The validator enforces the closed vocabulary for `domain` and `level`, integer `weight`, valid URLs, unique `id`s, and existing prerequisite references.
